body:
There was a miss here, there is no display on the settings page for the following work:

>
> **Assessment: Looks good**
>
> The feature does what the task asks. Keys are stored by model id in `keys.json`, written through a 0600 temp file and renamed into place. They never go in `config.toml` and the page never gets them back. A stored key wins over `key_env` for both Codex (`SOLACE_ENDPOINT_KEY`, set only on the agent's process) and Claude (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`). `local()` treats a stored key as available, and a model with no key stays in the list with its reason. The new routes go through the server's existing Host/Origin check, so another website can't post to `/models`.
>
> #### Findings (worth a follow-up, none blocking)
>
> - **Saving can drop a hand-written `run` command** (`setup.rs::save`, `entry.remove("run")`). The page lists every configured model, including ones defined by a custom `run` or ones that only override a preset's effort. Saving such a model from the page quietly turns it into an endpoint model and removes its `run`. Either list only endpoint models as editable, or warn before replacing.
> - **An id from a label can replace a built-in model.** A model labelled "Codex" gets the id `codex`, and a configured model replaces the preset with the same id. Refusing ids that match a preset, or adding a suffix, would avoid this surprise.
> - **Both files are rewritten through the same helper, `replace()`.** Because of that, `config.toml` also ends up 0600 after a save. That's harmless, but different from before. Comments in `config.toml` are lost on save; the work note already says so.
> - **Small inconsistency:** `has_key` in `GET /models` counts an empty-string key as saved, but `stored()` ignores empty keys. Today only non-empty keys get saved, so this doesn't show up in practice.
> - **Not done (stated in the work note):** Test connection, the keychain and Windows storage, and the Knowledgebase guide text.
>
> #### Verification
>
> - `rust-board-tests`: 89 passed.
> - Settings `test --all`: 8 passed. No test reaches `settings.init`.
> - The new tests cover saving, editing with a blank key, deleting, refused input, `env_key` with a stored key, and `local()` with a stored key, a missing one and a keyless endpoint.
> - **Not run:** `rust-unit`, `rust-acceptance`, the Settings `js_tests`, a real browser session (Save, Delete, the confirm dialog) and a real Command Code launch.
>
> Delete**agent · work · claude-opus-5-5 · low · claude-opus-5-5**10/17/2026, 9:07:47 PM
>
> #### Outcome
>
> You can now set up a model and its API key from the Settings page, without a command line. The key is kept in `~/.config/solace/keys.json`, which only you can read, as you chose. It never goes in `config.toml` and the page never shows it again.
>
> #### What changed
>
> - **Settings page** (`settings.gleam`, plus a small `api.mjs` for its server calls; `gleam_json` added to its `gleam.toml`): a new **Models** section.
>   - It lists the models you've set up, each with why it can't start, such as "No key yet; add one in Settings".
>   - A form adds or edits a model: label, agent (Codex or Claude Code), model id, endpoint base URL and API key.
>   - The key field always starts empty. When a key is saved it says "Key saved; leave blank to keep it".
>   - Delete asks you to confirm, then removes the model and its key.
> - **Server** (new `board/setup.rs`, routes in `board.rs`):
>   - `POST /models` adds or updates the entry in `config.toml`, checks the new settings before writing, and stores the key separately.
>   - `DELETE /models/<id>` removes the entry and its key.
>   - `GET /models` now also tells the page whether a key is saved, but never sends the key.
> - **Launch:** a saved key wins over the environment variable. Codex gets it through its own variable, set only on the agent's process. Claude Code gets it as its auth token. Models that name a key variable in `config.toml` (`key_env`) keep working.
> - **Availability** (`agents::local`): a saved key counts as available. A missing key now reads "No key yet; add one in Settings", or "…or set the variable X" for a model that names one. An endpoint that names no key, such as a local server, still needs none.
> - **Docs:** a new decision record, D-164, and a Models section in the Settings README.
>
> #### Verification
>
> All of these pass:
>
> - `rust-board-tests`: 89
> - `rust-unit`: 409
> - `rust-acceptance`: 125
> - Settings `test --all`: 8
> - Settings `js_tests`: 4
>
> New tests cover:
>
> - Saving a model, editing it with a blank key (the saved key stays), and deleting it.
> - `keys.json` being readable only by you, and the key never appearing in `config.toml`.
> - Refused input: missing fields, an unknown agent, a label with no letters or digits.
> - A saved key, a missing key and a keyless endpoint, plus how each key reaches Codex.
> - The page's list, form and error message.
>
> #### Things to know
>
> - **Comments are lost:** saving from Settings rewrites `config.toml`, so any comments in it are dropped.
> - **Keyless endpoints:** a model added from Settings always expects a key. A local endpoint that needs none has to be set up in `config.toml` directly for now.
> - **Not checked by hand:** nobody has used the page in a real browser yet. That includes Save and Delete, the confirm dialog, and a real Command Code run.
> - **Also check:** the shell's bundled `app.js` gets rebuilt in the build plan, so check the page after the next build.
> - **Not built:**
>   - **Test connection:** reaching https endpoints needs a TLS client, which would be a new dependency.
>   - **Keychain storage:** left out for now, as you chose.
>   - **Windows:** your note about the credential manager or a user-only ACL is recorded in D-164 for later. Solace's launch code is Unix-only today anyway.
> - **Knowledgebase guide:** not updated, because the frontend project is outside this task.
